questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Which feature is needed for a binomial situation?

answer.text: Each trial has success or failure

feedback.text: Binomial situations count successes across repeated success/failure trials.

answer.text: Every outcome has more than two categories

feedback.text: Binomial trials have two categories.

answer.text: There is no fixed number of trials

feedback.text: A fixed number of trials is required.
The probability of success should stay the same.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

In the formula expected successes = n × p, what is n?

feedback.text: n represents how many repeated trials occur.
That is p.
n includes all trials, not only failures.
n is a count, not a percent.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

A website has 200 visitors, and each visitor has probability 0.05 of clicking an ad. What is the expected number of clicks?

feedback.text: This is the probability of one click, not expected clicks.
This would come from 100 visitors, not 200.
This assumes every visitor clicks.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Which context is not binomial?

answer.text: Counting how many of 12 parts are defective

feedback.text: Each part can be defective or not defective.

answer.text: Counting how many of 20 customers use a coupon

feedback.text: Each customer can use or not use a coupon.

answer.text: Measuring the exact time each runner takes

feedback.text: Exact time is not a success/failure outcome.

answer.text: Counting how many of 15 shots are made

feedback.text: Each shot can be made or missed.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

A machine has probability 0.02 of producing a defective item. In 100 items, what is the expected number defective?

feedback.text: This is the probability for one item.
This would use 0.20 instead of 0.02.
This assumes every item is defective.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

What does success mean in a binomial situation?

feedback.text: Success only means the outcome being counted; it may not be good.
The number of trials is n.
Success is defined by the context.
That describes expected value.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

A sales team contacts 40 people. Each has probability 0.25 of responding. What is the expected number of responses?

feedback.text: This uses 0.10 instead of 0.25.
This uses 0.20 instead of 0.25.
This assumes every person responds.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Why is "favorite lunch item" usually not a binomial trial?

feedback.text: Student contexts can be binomial if there are two outcomes.
The issue is categories, not numbers.
It can be surveyed, but it is not automatically binomial.

answer.text: It has more than two possible categories

feedback.text: A binomial trial has only success or failure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

A quiz has 30 questions and the chance of a correct answer is 0.60 for each question. What is n?

feedback.text: This is p, not n.
There are 30 trials.
This is the expected number correct.
This confuses 0.60 with 60 trials.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

For 30 questions with probability 0.60 correct, what is the expected number correct?

feedback.text: This is the probability for one question.
This assumes all answers are correct.
This treats the probability as a count.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

What does failure mean in a binomial situation?

answer.text: The situation did not work mathematically

feedback.text: Failure is a category, not a math error.
Failures are part of the binomial count.
Probabilities cannot be negative.

answer.text: The outcome that is not counted as success

feedback.text: Each trial is either success or failure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Which values identify a binomial expected value calculation?

feedback.text: Those are summary statistics, not the binomial expected value inputs.
Expected successes are found with n × p.
Those belong to linear models.
Those are measurement terms, not binomial expected value inputs.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

A player attempts 50 free throws with success probability 0.72. What is the expected number made?

feedback.text: This is p, not expected successes.
This assumes every shot is made.
This treats 72% as 72 makes.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Which interpretation is strongest for an expected value of 36 made shots?

answer.text: Exactly 36 shots must be made every time

feedback.text: Expected value is not a guarantee.

answer.text: The player cannot make more than 36

feedback.text: Expected value is not a maximum.

answer.text: Over many sets of 50 shots, the average made should be about 36

feedback.text: This explains long-run average behavior.

answer.text: The probability of one made shot is 36

feedback.text: A probability cannot be 36.

Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

What is expected successes when n = 80 and p = 0.10?

feedback.text: This is p, not expected successes.
This would use p = 0.05.

Which situation violates the fixed-trials condition?

feedback.text: This has a fixed number of trials.

answer.text: Asking exactly 100 people a yes/no question

feedback.text: This has a fixed number of trials.
The number of trials is not fixed in advance.
This has a fixed number of trials.

Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

If p = 0.30, what does that mean?

answer.text: The probability of success on one trial is 0.30

feedback.text: p is the single-trial success probability.
That would describe n, not p.
p does not guarantee a count.
Expected successes also depend on n.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Expected successes for n = 12 and p = 0.25 equals what?

feedback.text: This is p.
This assumes all trials succeed.

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Which statement about binomial expected value is true?

answer.text: It guarantees the exact number of successes

feedback.text: Expected value is not a guarantee.

answer.text: It uses both number of trials and probability of success

feedback.text: Expected successes = n × p.

answer.text: It ignores the number of trials

feedback.text: The formula uses n.
The formula works for any valid p.

A company expects 4% of 500 emails to receive replies. What is the expected number of replies?

feedback.text: This treats 4% as 4 replies without using 500.

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

feedback.text: The success is the outcome being counted.
That is the failure if sprouting is being counted.

Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

If 25 seeds each have probability 0.80 of sprouting, what is expected successes?

feedback.text: This is one-trial probability.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Why is "number of red cards in 5 draws with replacement" binomial if success is red?

feedback.text: The defined outcome is red or not red, so each trial has two categories.

answer.text: Each draw can be classified as red or not red, and the probability stays the same with replacement

feedback.text: Replacement keeps the probability of success constant.
The number of draws is fixed at 5.
Expected successes can be calculated with n × p.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

What is expected red cards in 5 draws with replacement if p(red) = 0.50?

feedback.text: This is p, not the expected count.
This is too low for 5 trials at 0.50.
5 × 0.50 = 2.5 expected red cards.
This assumes all draws are red.

Question ID: STAT_U06_L04_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.STAT.PSU.14

Which final answer best explains a binomial expected value of 2.5?

answer.text: Exactly 2.5 successes must occur in one set

feedback.text: A single set cannot have half a success.
Expected successes are not the number of trials.
A probability cannot be greater than 1.

answer.text: The average number of successes should be about 2.5 over many repeated sets of trials

feedback.text: This is the long-run interpretation.
